adopt.note.stale_inconsistent_default: the notes in {dir} do not agree on how long until they go stale, so its stale policy stays this language's default of {months} months.
adopt.note.stale_default_kept: {dir} goes stale after {months} months, this language's default: no note there carries both stale_after and generated.at.
adopt.note.stale_none: no folder has a stale policy: no notes agree on one, and no folder has this language's default.
update.usage:
Usage: brain-kit update [dir] [--check]
       brain-kit update [dir] --accept <path>
       brain-kit update [dir] --install-hook

Refreshes the files the kit manages in the vault found from dir (default: the current directory), by checksum, as .brain-kit/manifest.json records them. A managed file you have not edited is replaced with this kit's version. A managed file you edited is never overwritten: when this kit has a newer version, it is written beside it as <name>.brain-kit-new for you to take what you want from. A seeded note is yours and is never touched. A managed file you deleted is reported and not recreated. Line endings are kept as each file has them. After a run with no failed write, the configuration's kit_version is set to this kit's version.

  --check          write nothing; exit 1 when anything would change or needs you, 0 otherwise
  --accept <path>  you have dealt with this kit's version of a managed file (path relative to the vault): remember it, so it is not offered again until the kit changes it, and remove its .brain-kit-new; your file is not touched. For a managed file you deleted on purpose, stop tracking it.
  --install-hook   install the push gate: .githooks/pre-push from this kit's template, core.hooksPath, and its manifest entry. A hook of your own, or a core.hooksPath pointing elsewhere, is left exactly as it is, and you are told how to add the gate to it. Exit 0 installed or already there, 3 left as it was, 1 not possible here.

It refuses, writing nothing, when the manifest cannot be read, when this kit is older than the configuration's kit_version, and when the configuration's lang is not the language the managed files were written in.

Exit codes: 0 everything current, 1 failure or (with --check) something pending, 2 usage or not inside a vault, 3 done but something needs you.
update.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit update: "{dir}" is not a directory.
update.no_vault: brain-kit update: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and index.md).
update.manifest_unreadable:
brain-kit update: {detail}
Nothing was written. Without a readable manifest update cannot tell the kit's files from yours, so it refuses rather than treat the vault as having nothing to update. If the vault has a commit that holds it, git checkout -- .brain-kit/manifest.json brings it back.
update.would_refresh: Would update {file} to this kit's version.
update.offered: {file} was edited, so it was left as it is. This kit's version was written beside it as {new}. Take what you want from it into your file, then run: {command}
update.would_offer: {file} was edited, so it would be left as it is, and this kit's version would be written beside it as {new}.
update.offer_blocked: {file} was edited and this kit has a newer version of it, but {new} is already there, so nothing was written. Take what you want from it into your file, then run: {command}
update.missing: {file} is managed by the kit but no longer exists; it was not recreated. If you removed it on purpose, run: {command}
update.not_regular: {file} is not a regular file inside the vault (it is a link, a directory, or reached through a linked directory), so it was left alone.
update.unreadable: {file} could not be read ({detail}), so it was left alone.
update.kept: {file} was edited; this kit has nothing newer for it, so it was left as it is.
update.not_in_kit: {file} is managed, but this kit no longer ships it; it was left as it is.
update.raced: {file} changed while update was running, so it was left as it is. Run brain-kit update again.
update.manifest_write_failed: brain-kit update: .brain-kit/manifest.json could not be rewritten ({detail}), so the hashes of any file updated above are the old ones: those files read as current, but a later kit version will be offered beside them instead of replacing them.
update.summary: {managed} managed file(s): {refreshed} updated, {current} already current, {kept} edited and kept, {attention} needing you; {seeded} seeded note(s) left alone.
update.check_pending: {count} file(s) pending: run brain-kit update to apply what it can, and see above for what needs you.
update.accept_with_check: brain-kit update: --accept writes the manifest, and --check writes nothing; use one or the other.
update.install_hook_alone: brain-kit update: --install-hook runs on its own; it cannot be combined with --check or --accept.
update.check_summary: {managed} managed file(s): {refreshed} would be updated, {current} already current, {kept} edited and kept, {attention} needing you; {seeded} seeded note(s) left alone.
update.kit_older: brain-kit update: this kit is {running}, older than the {configured} this vault's configuration was written for, so it would put back older versions of the kit's files. Nothing was written. Update brain-kit, then run this again.
update.lang_changed: brain-kit update: the kit's files in this vault were written in {recorded}, and the configuration now says lang is {configured}. Their language is fixed when the vault is made: refreshing them from the other language would replace every contract file with one whose links point at folders this vault does not have. Nothing was written. Set lang back to update them.
update.manifest_not_regular: brain-kit update: {file} is not a regular file (a link, or something else), so update will not write it. Nothing was written.
update.manifest_outside: brain-kit update: {file} is reached through a link that leads outside the vault, so update will not write it. Nothing was written.
update.manifest_not_writable: brain-kit update: {dir} is not writable, so the manifest could not be updated after the files were. Nothing was written.
update.config_not_editable: brain-kit update: this kit is newer than the kit_version in {file}, but that file is not a regular file holding exactly one kit_version update can set. Nothing was written.
update.bumped: Set kit_version in the configuration from {from} to {to}.
update.would_bump: Would set kit_version in the configuration from {from} to {to}.
update.accept_outside: brain-kit update: "{path}" is not a file inside the vault.
update.accept_not_managed: brain-kit update: {file} is not a file the kit manages, so there is nothing to accept.
update.accept_not_executable: brain-kit update: {file} is not executable, and git skips a hook it cannot execute, so accepting it would leave the vault with no gate. Nothing was written. Run {command}, then accept it again.
update.accept_recorded: Recorded this kit's version of {file}: it will not be offered again until the kit changes it. Your file was not touched.
update.accept_dropped: {file} is no longer tracked by update.
update.accept_new_left: {new} is a directory, so it was left where it is.
update.accept_nothing: {file} has nothing to accept: the manifest already records this kit's version of it, and there is nothing beside it.
update.accept_last_entry: brain-kit update: {file} is the last file the manifest lists, and a manifest cannot be empty. Nothing was written.
init.gitignore_update: Written by brain-kit update: versions offered beside a file you edited, and temporary files a stopped run can leave.
guard.not_a_repository: {dir} is not inside a git working tree. This command changes a vault only through git, so the vault must be a repository. Nothing was written.
guard.git_failed: git could not answer about {dir}: {detail}. Nothing was written.
lock.held: Another run is changing this vault: pid {pid} on {host} ({command}, since {startedAt}). Postponed; run again when it ends.
lock.held_unreadable: The vault lock {lock} cannot be read, so whoever holds it cannot be proved gone. Postponed. If no brain-kit run is active on this vault, remove that file.
lock.reclaim_died: A run that was replacing a dead holder's lock died midway and left {marker} behind. No run can take the lock until that file is removed; remove it and run again.
lock.no_hard_links: The file system holding {dir} does not support hard links, which the vault lock needs to be taken safely. Keep the vault on a file system that has them (ext4, APFS, NTFS and most local file systems do). Nothing was written.
snapshot.not_toplevel: {dir} is inside the repository at {top}, not its top level. Run from the vault's top level. Nothing was written.
snapshot.other_root: The session snapshot was taken of {snapshotRoot}, not of {dir}. It cannot say which of this tree's changes came before the session.
snapshot.unreadable: {file} is not a session snapshot this version can read. Remove it and start the session again.
sync.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit sync: "{dir}" is not a directory.
sync.no_vault: brain-kit sync: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
sync.operation_in_progress: A {operation} is in progress in this working tree, so sync postponed without fetching or moving anything. Finish it or abort it, then run again.
sync.dirty: The working tree has changes that are not committed ({files}), so sync postponed without fetching or moving anything. Commit, move or remove them, then run again.
sync.no_default_branch: No default branch is known: {file} sets no vault.default_branch, and neither remote {remote} (HEAD, main, master) nor a local main or master names one. Set it there. Nothing was changed.
sync.default_branch_invalid: vault.default_branch in {file} is "{name}", which is not a branch name. Nothing was changed.
sync.no_remote: The default branch {branch} is brought up to date from remote {remote}, and this repository has no remote by that name. Nothing was changed.
sync.fetch_failed: Could not fetch {branch} from remote {remote}, so whether the local branch is behind it is NOT known. Nothing was changed. git said: {detail}
sync.fetch_incomplete: git fetch from remote {remote} reported success, but {upstream} does not hold {sha}, the tip the remote announced for {branch}: the fetch reached nothing usable, so whether the local branch is behind it is NOT known. Nothing was changed.
sync.remote_has_no_branch: Remote {remote} has no branch {branch} yet (nothing is published there), so there is nothing to bring in. Nothing was changed.
sync.local_upstream: The default branch {branch} tracks a branch of this same repository ({key} is "."), not a remote, so sync will not bring it level with any remote's history. Point it at the remote branch it publishes to (git branch --set-upstream-to=<remote>/<branch>), then run again. Nothing was changed.
sync.remote_lacks_branch: Remote {remote} does not publish {branch}: it publishes {published} (its HEAD: {head}), so there is something there and this is not "nothing to bring in". A default renamed on the forge, a typo in vault.default_branch, or master against main. Set vault.default_branch in {file} to the branch the remote publishes, or run: {command}. Nothing was changed.
sync.no_local_branch: There is no local branch {branch} to bring level with {upstream}. Create it with: {command}. Nothing was changed.
sync.up_to_date: {branch} is level with {upstream}: 0 ahead, 0 behind. Nothing to bring in.
sync.ahead: {branch} is {ahead} ahead of {upstream} and 0 behind: nothing to bring in. Nothing was changed.
sync.diverged: {branch} and {upstream} have diverged: {ahead} ahead and {behind} behind. Nothing was changed. Reconcile the two by hand before anything is written.
sync.ignored_in_the_way: Bringing {branch} level with {upstream} would overwrite files git ignores here ({files}), which may be another session's work, so sync postponed without moving anything. Move them aside, then run again.
sync.fast_forwarded: {branch} was {behind} behind {upstream} and 0 ahead: fast-forwarded from {from} to {to}.
sync.checkout_failed: Could not check out {branch} to fast-forward it, so it was not moved. git said: {detail}
sync.fast_forward_failed: Could not fast-forward {branch} to {upstream}; check where it points before anything is written. git said: {detail}
sync.return_failed: Could not return to {start}, where sync started: the repository is left on {current}. Check out the starting branch by hand before anything else runs.
sync.git_failed: brain-kit sync: git could not answer, so nothing more was done: {detail}
machine.usage:
Usage: brain-kit machine show [dir]
       brain-kit machine set <key> <value> [dir]
       brain-kit machine register [dir] [--from <previous vault path>]
machine.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit machine: "{dir}" is not a directory.
machine.no_vault: brain-kit machine: no brain-kit vault found at "{dir}" or in any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
machine.missing: brain-kit machine: no machine.json at {file}. If this vault was moved, run: brain-kit machine register --from <its previous path>. On a machine that never had it, run: brain-kit init --adopt.
machine.unreadable: brain-kit machine: {file} is not JSON this command can read: {error}
machine.invalid: brain-kit machine: {file} is not a valid machine file: {errors}
machine.set_unknown_key: brain-kit machine set: "{key}" is not a machine.json key. The keys are: {keys}, and paths.<name> for a name the schema declares under paths.
machine.set_managed_key: brain-kit machine set: {key} is written by brain-kit init and moved only by brain-kit machine register; it cannot be set by hand. Nothing was written.
machine.set_needs_array: brain-kit machine set: {key} takes a JSON array, one element per argument, like ["notify-send", "done"]; "{value}" is not one. Nothing was written.
machine.set_needs_object: brain-kit machine set: {key} takes a JSON object; "{value}" is not one. Nothing was written.
machine.set_needs_integer: brain-kit machine set: {key} takes a whole number; "{value}" is not one. Nothing was written.
machine.set_needs_boolean: brain-kit machine set: {key} takes true or false; "{value}" is neither. Nothing was written.
machine.set_rejected: brain-kit machine set: {key} was not changed, because the result would not be a valid machine file: {errors}. {file} was left as it was.
machine.register_nothing: brain-kit machine register: no machine.json at {file}, which is where this path's state belongs. If this vault was moved, run again with --from <its previous path>; register never guesses which state was this vault's.
machine.register_candidates:
State directories whose vault is no longer where their machine.json says:
{list}
machine.register_from_missing: brain-kit machine register: no machine.json at {file}, the state directory {from} would have had on this machine. Nothing was moved.
machine.register_source_live: brain-kit machine register: {file} belongs to the vault at {vault}, which is still there. A copy of a vault is not a move: give the copy its own state with brain-kit init --adopt. Nothing was moved.
machine.register_target_unreadable: brain-kit machine register: {file} already exists and cannot be read ({error}), so it cannot be proved to be this vault's. It was not overwritten, and nothing was moved.
machine.register_target_not_empty: brain-kit machine register: {dir} already holds files but no machine.json, so they cannot be proved to be this vault's. Nothing was moved.
machine.register_done: Registered this vault at {dir}: its state moved from {from} to {to}.
machine.register_stranded: brain-kit machine register: writing the machine file failed after the state moved to {to}, and moving it back failed too. Move that directory back to {from} by hand.
machine.other_vault: brain-kit machine: {file} records the vault at {vault}, which is still there, not this one. The state directory is pinned by BRAIN_KIT_STATE_DIR or shared; point it at this vault's own. Nothing was written.
machine.state_inside_vault: brain-kit machine: the state directory {state} is inside the vault {dir}, where it would be committed. Point BRAIN_KIT_STATE_DIR or XDG_STATE_HOME outside it. Nothing was written.
machine.show_path_differs: brain-kit machine: this record was written for {recorded}, not for {dir} where the vault is now. Run brain-kit machine register to record the move.
machine.register_target_invalid: brain-kit machine register: {file} already exists and is not a valid machine file ({errors}), so it cannot be proved to be this vault's. It was not overwritten, and nothing was moved.
machine.register_target_taken: brain-kit machine register: {file} already holds the state of vault {theirs}, while {source} holds the state of vault {ours}. A path is not an identity: neither was touched, and nothing was moved.
machine.register_already: This vault is already registered at {dir}: {file}. Nothing to do.
watermark.usage:
Usage: brain-kit watermark show [dir]
       brain-kit watermark set <source> <YYYY-MM-DD> [dir]
       brain-kit watermark reopen <source> <YYYY-MM-DD> [dir]
       brain-kit watermark assume-covered <source> [dir]
watermark.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit watermark: "{dir}" is not a directory.
watermark.no_vault: brain-kit watermark: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
watermark.unreadable: brain-kit watermark: the watermark file {file} cannot be read ({detail}). Nothing was changed. Fix it by hand (it holds {"sources": {"<source>": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}); removing it instead makes every source read only yesterday on the next round, closing any other open day unread.
watermark.show_header: High water mark ({file}), days in {timezone}; yesterday was {yesterday}.
watermark.show_unset: {source}: not set (the next round reads only yesterday)
watermark.show_line: {source}: last day swept {day}, {behind} day(s) behind yesterday
watermark.unknown_source: brain-kit watermark: "{source}" is not a source of this vault. Known sources: {sources}.
watermark.bad_date: brain-kit watermark: "{value}" is not a date written as YYYY-MM-DD.
watermark.future_date: brain-kit watermark: {day} has not ended yet in {timezone}; the latest day a mark can hold is yesterday, {yesterday}. Nothing was changed.
watermark.already_open: brain-kit watermark: {day} is already open for {source} (last day swept: {mark}); the next round reads it. Nothing was changed.
watermark.unchanged: {source}: the last day swept is already {day}. Nothing was changed.
watermark.moved: {source}: last day swept moved from {from} to {to}.
watermark.skipped: Days now closed without having been read by a round ({count}): {days}.
watermark.beyond_clip: Note: {count} days are open, and a round reads at most {max}, oldest first; the rounds after it continue until the mark reaches yesterday.
watermark.show_future: {source}: last day swept {day}, {ahead} day(s) AHEAD of yesterday ({yesterday}). No round can have swept a day that has not ended: a clock ran ahead, and rounds refuse to run until this is fixed. Reopen from the first day that was not really read, for example: {command}
watermark.bad_timezone: brain-kit watermark: vault.timezone in {file} is "{timezone}", which is not a time zone this system knows (use an IANA name such as America/New_York or Asia/Tokyo). Nothing was changed.
verify.usage:
Usage: brain-kit verify --pr <number> [dir]
       brain-kit verify --files <path>...

The owner's command, after merging the agent's pull request: stamps verified (by actors.human from the configuration, at the current time) on every note the merged pull request changed, or on the notes listed, commits the stamps with your own git identity and prints the push command. It runs on the default branch with a clean tree, and refuses the agent's identity.
verify.both_modes: brain-kit verify: give either --pr or --files, not both.
verify.no_mode: brain-kit verify: say what to verify: --pr <number> or --files <path>...
verify.bad_pr: brain-kit verify: --pr takes a pull request number, and "{value}" is not one.
verify.no_files: brain-kit verify: --files takes at least one path.
verify.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit verify: "{dir}" is not a directory.
verify.no_vault: brain-kit verify: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
verify.operation_in_progress: A {operation} is in progress in this working tree, and a commit now would conclude it, so verify postponed without writing anything. Finish it or abort it, then run again.
verify.dirty: The working tree has changes that are not committed ({files}), so verify postponed without writing anything: its commit must hold the stamps and nothing else. Commit, move or remove them, then run again.
verify.no_default_branch: No default branch is known (set vault.default_branch in {file}), so verify cannot tell where the stamps belong. Nothing was written.
verify.default_branch_invalid: vault.default_branch in {file} is "{name}", which is not a branch name. Nothing was written.
verify.not_on_default: verify runs on the default branch {branch}, and this checkout is on {current}. Check it out, then run again. Nothing was written.
verify.detached: verify runs on the default branch {branch}, and this checkout is on a detached HEAD. Check it out, then run again. Nothing was written.
verify.identity_unknown: git cannot say which identity the commit would carry, so verify stopped before writing anything. Set user.name and user.email with git config, then run again. git said: {detail}
verify.agent_identity: The commit would carry {name} <{email}>, which is the agent's identity (git.agent_identity in {file}). The agent never verifies its own work: the owner runs verify, with the owner's own git identity. Nothing was written.
verify.gh_failed: gh could not read pull request #{pr}, so nothing is known about it and nothing was written. gh said: {detail}
verify.gh_unreadable: gh answered about pull request #{pr} in a shape verify cannot read (a state, a baseRefName and a list of files with their paths were expected), so nothing was written: {detail}
verify.pr_not_merged: Pull request #{pr} is {state}, not merged. Only the merge is the owner's approval: merge it first. Nothing was written.
verify.pr_wrong_base: Pull request #{pr} was merged into {base}, not into the default branch {branch}, so it is not approved work on this vault. Nothing was written.
verify.pr_no_files: gh lists no file for pull request #{pr}, although it is merged: that is an answer about nothing, not "nothing to verify". Check the pull request, or name the notes with --files. Nothing was written.
verify.pr_too_many_files: gh lists {count} files for pull request #{pr}, and it lists at most the first {limit} files of a pull request, so notes could be skipped without a word. Name the notes with --files instead. Nothing was written.
verify.local_upstream: The default branch {branch} tracks a branch of this same repository, not a remote, so verify cannot prove the merge is in this checkout. Nothing was written.
verify.remote_unproven: Could not fetch {branch} from remote {remote}, so whether the merge is in this checkout is NOT known. Nothing was written. ({detail})
verify.behind: {branch} is {behind} behind {upstream}: the merge may not be in this checkout yet, and a note it added would be missed. Run brain-kit sync, then verify again. Nothing was written.
verify.file_outside: brain-kit verify: {path} is outside this vault. Nothing was written.
verify.file_gone: brain-kit verify: {path} does not exist. Nothing was written.
verify.file_not_note: brain-kit verify: {path} is not a note of this vault (a markdown file the vault's walk includes and git tracks, not index.md, log.md or a template). Nothing was written.
verify.skipped_gone: Skipped {path}: no longer exists (deleted by the pull request or since).
verify.skipped_not_note: Skipped {path}: not a note (not markdown, ignored, reserved, a template, or not tracked by git).
verify.nothing_to_stamp: No note of this vault among the files of pull request #{pr}: nothing to stamp, and nothing was written.
verify.refused_encoding: {path} is not UTF-8 text, so it cannot be stamped without changing other bytes.
verify.refused_no_frontmatter: {path} has no frontmatter block, so it is not a note and cannot be stamped.
verify.refused_unreadable: {path} has verified (or a frontmatter) in a shape brain-kit cannot read, so it was not rewritten. Write verified as a list of by: and at: entries by hand, then run again.
verify.refused_duplicate: {path} has the verified key more than once, so it was not rewritten.
verify.refused_incomplete: {path} has a verification event without a by or without an at, so it was not rewritten. Give each entry both, then run again.
verify.refused_bad_value: The actor or the time to stamp on {path} is not a value verify can write (actors.human must be an actor such as human:ana).
verify.nothing_written: Nothing was written, in any note.
verify.changed_underneath: {path} changed while verify was writing, so every note was put back as it was and nothing was committed.
verify.write_failed: Could not write {path} ({detail}), so every note was put back as it was and nothing was committed.
verify.restore_failed: Could not put back {files} as they were: check them by hand.
verify.commit_failed: git could not commit the stamps, so every note was put back as it was. git said: {detail}
verify.commit_unproven: The commit on {branch} cannot be proved to hold exactly the stamps (one new commit on it, only the stamped notes, a clean tree after it); the checkout is now on {current}. Check it with git log -1 --stat before pushing.
verify.failed: brain-kit verify: stopped, and nothing more was done: {detail}
verify.commit_pr: verify: pull request #{pr} merged into {branch}, {count} note(s) verified by {by}
verify.remote_not_github: The default branch tracks remote {remote}, whose URL ({url}) names no GitHub repository verify can hand gh as --repo, so which pull request #n is cannot be known. Nothing was written.
verify.merge_not_pulled: Pull request #{pr} was merged as {sha}, which {upstream} holds and the local {branch} (at {tip}) does not: the merge is not in this checkout yet. Run brain-kit sync, then verify again. Nothing was written.
verify.merge_not_here: gh reports pull request #{pr} of {repo} merged as {sha}, and that commit is in neither the local {branch} (at {tip}) nor {upstream}: it is not this history's merge, so nothing is stamped. Nothing was written.
verify.unreadable: {path} cannot be read here ({detail}), so it cannot be stamped.
propose.usage:
Usage: brain-kit propose "<summary>" (--only <path>... | --all [--yes]) [--dry] [-- <argument>...]
  The summary comes first, before --only; --only takes every argument after it up to the next option. After --, nothing is read as an option: the first argument is the summary if none was given yet, and the rest are --only paths, so a summary or a path beginning with - goes there. The vault is the one the current directory is in.
propose.bad_argument: brain-kit propose: unknown or repeated argument "{arg}".
propose.no_summary: brain-kit propose: a summary is required, as the first argument, and it cannot be blank.
propose.mode_required: brain-kit propose: give exactly one of --only <path>... (the normal path) or --all.
propose.only_empty: brain-kit propose: --only names no path. List every path to propose after it.
propose.yes_without_all: brain-kit propose: --yes only confirms --all. With --only, the paths you list are the confirmation.
propose.no_vault: brain-kit propose: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
propose.not_toplevel: brain-kit propose: the vault at {dir} is inside a larger repository (at "{prefix}" below its top level), and propose only works on a vault that is the top level of its own repository. Nothing was changed.
propose.operation_in_progress: A {operation} is in progress in this working tree, so propose postponed without reading or moving anything. Finish or abort it, then run again.
propose.nothing_to_propose: Nothing to propose: the working tree is clean.
propose.outside_vault: These paths are outside the vault at {dir}, so nothing was proposed: {paths}.
propose.not_dirty: These paths have no change to propose (not modified, not new, not deleted, or ignored by git), so nothing was proposed: {paths}. Name only the paths this session changed.
propose.no_snapshot: --all refused: there is no session snapshot, so which changed files were already there before this session (another session's work, possibly) cannot be told. Propose your own paths with --only, or confirm the whole tree with --all --yes. Nothing was changed.
propose.stale_snapshot: --all refused: the session snapshot was taken at {at}, more than a day ago or in the future, so it cannot tell this session's files from another's. Propose your own paths with --only, or confirm the whole tree with --all --yes. Nothing was changed.
propose.dirty_before: --all refused: these files were already changed when the session began ({at}), and may be another session's unfinished work: {files}. Propose your own paths with --only, or confirm them with --all --yes. Nothing was changed.
propose.validate_failed: Nothing was proposed: validate failed (exit {code}) on the working tree. Fix the findings above, then run again.
propose.lint_failed: Nothing was proposed: lint --base worktree failed (exit {code}). Fix the findings above, then run again.
propose.no_default_branch: No default branch is known to propose against: {file} sets no vault.default_branch, and neither remote {remote} (HEAD, main, master) nor a local main or master names one. Set it there. Nothing was changed.
propose.default_branch_invalid: vault.default_branch in {file} is "{name}", which is not a branch name, so there is no base to propose against. Nothing was changed.
propose.local_upstream: The default branch {branch} tracks a branch of this same repository ({key} is "."), not a remote, so there is no remote base to propose against. Point it at the remote branch it publishes to, then run again. Nothing was changed.
propose.no_remote: The default branch {branch} is published to remote {remote}, and this repository has no remote by that name. Nothing was changed.
propose.branch_invalid: The branch this proposal would be pushed to, "{branch}", is not a usable branch name (check git.branch_prefix). Nothing was changed.
propose.dry_run: Dry run, nothing changed and nothing fetched. Would propose {files} as "{title}", pushed to {urls} as {branch}, in a pull request against {base}. HEAD stays on {origin}.
propose.remote_has_no_branch: Remote {remote} publishes no branch at all yet, so there is no {branch} to propose against. Push the default branch first. Nothing was changed.
propose.remote_lacks_branch: Remote {remote} does not publish {branch}, the base this proposal would target: it publishes {published}. Set vault.default_branch to the branch the remote publishes. Nothing was changed.
propose.fetch_failed: Could not fetch {branch} from remote {remote}, so the base this proposal would be built on is NOT known. Nothing was changed. git said: {detail}
propose.fetch_incomplete: git fetch of {branch} from remote {remote} reported success, but the fetched reference does not hold the tip the remote announced, so the base is NOT known. Nothing was changed.
propose.base_differs: These paths are not the same at HEAD as at {base} ({tip}), so their changes were made on a version the base does not hold, and proposing them would revert or carry that difference: {files}. Bring the branch level with that base (brain-kit sync) and redo the change on top of it. Nothing was changed.
propose.body_outside: git.pr_body is "{file}", which is outside the vault. Nothing was changed.
propose.body_unreadable: The pull request body template {file} could not be read ({detail}). Nothing was changed.
propose.tree_mismatch: The proposal's tree does not change exactly the chosen paths (chosen: {expected}; changed: {actual}), so nothing was pushed.
propose.push_failed: The push of {branch} failed, and every push url ({urls}) answered that it does not hold it, so nothing was published and the working tree still holds every change; run again. git said: {detail}
propose.push_unproved: The push of {branch} reported success, but no push url ({urls}) holds {commit} there, so nothing is known to be published. Check the remote before running again.
propose.degraded_create: The commit is pushed as {branch}, but the pull request was not opened: {detail}. Open it by hand with: {command}
propose.degraded_view: The commit is pushed as {branch} and a pull request was requested, but its base could not be confirmed: {detail}. Check it with: {command}
propose.degraded_base: The pull request for {branch} was opened as {found}, not against {base}. Fix its base with: {command}
propose.opened: Pull request opened against {base} from {branch}, {count} file(s): {url}. HEAD is still on {origin}, and the index and the working tree were not touched.
propose.git_failed: brain-kit propose stopped, and nothing more was done: {detail}
propose.partial_publish: {branch} is published to {held} but not to {missing} (not held, or no answer), so no pull request was opened. Finish by hand with: {command}
propose.round_record_failed: The commit is pushed as {branch}, but the record the round reads could not be written in {dir} ({code}), so the round will leave the proposed files in the working tree and report them.
propose.round_record_invalid: The commit is pushed as {branch}, but the record the round reads in {dir} is not one this version can read, so it was left as it is and this proposal is not in it; the round will leave the proposed files in the working tree and report them.
propose.pending: An earlier run published {branch} without a confirmed pull request. Finish it by hand with: {command}
propose.pending_unreadable: The record of an earlier proposal, {file}, cannot be read; check it and remove it by hand.
propose.nested_repository: These paths are a submodule pointer or a nested repository, which propose does not handle in this version, so nothing was proposed: {paths}.
propose.no_push_url: Remote {remote} has no configured push destination (no pushurl and no url), so there is nowhere to publish the proposal. Nothing was changed.
propose.url_rewritten: The push url {url} does not stay itself when git is asked about it (it resolves to "{got}"), so where the proposal would land cannot be proved. Nothing was changed.
propose.destination_unreadable: The push url {url} could not be asked which branches it holds, so no branch name can be chosen safely. Nothing was changed.
propose.branch_exhausted: {branch} and every suffix up to -9 already exist at the push destination. Nothing was changed; run again in a second.
prompt.usage:
Usage: brain-kit prompt skill <name> [--vault <dir>]
       brain-kit prompt curate [--vault <dir>]
       brain-kit prompt --check [--vault <dir>]

skill prints a skill's body, in the vault's own language, for the plugin's SKILL.md files to run through their "!" line. curate prints the prompt a scheduled curate round hands the model, the vault's own file at curate.prompt (.brain-kit/prompts/curate.md by default) when it exists. --check verifies that every skill the plugin ships has a body in both language packs, that both packs carry the same skill and prompt files with the same placeholders, that every placeholder used is known, and that every prompt carries its contract markers; it warns, without failing, when the vault's own curate prompt lacks one.
prompt.no_vault_notice: No brain-kit vault was found from {dir}: do not write any file; tell the person no vault was found here, and suggest opening the session inside the vault or running the setup skill.
prompt.body_unreadable: The body for the "{name}" skill could not be loaded. Run brain-kit doctor.
prompt.check_ok: brain-kit prompt --check: every skill and prompt is present in every supported language, both packs agree, every placeholder used is known, and every contract marker is in place.
prompt.check_dir_unreadable: {lang}: the skills directory could not be read ({dir}).
prompt.check_missing_body: {name} ({lang}): no body, and the plugin ships this skill.
prompt.check_pack_mismatch: {name}: has a body in {lang} but not in {other}.
prompt.check_body_unreadable: {name} ({lang}): the body could not be read ({detail}).
sources.transcripts.heading: Transcripts with a message between {from} and {to}: {count} files, newest first. Every time here is UTC; convert to the vault's time zone before dating anything. Read each one from its sample line (the line holding the start of the last {sample} KB) and earlier slices only if needed, never the whole file:
sources.transcripts.file_line: session {session}: {path} (project {project}, messages {firstAt}..{lastAt}, {bytes} bytes, read from byte {sampleFrom}, line {sampleLine})
sources.transcripts.none_in_window: No transcript has a message inside the window {from} to {to}.
sources.transcripts.unreadable_line: - {path} (project {project}, {bytes} bytes): could not be read or holds no message timestamp; reported here rather than dropped.
sources.transcripts.dropped_by_cap: {count} transcripts left out by the cap of {cap}.
sources.transcripts.dropped_self_trace: {count} transcripts left out as the curator's own runs (their first message starts with a curator signature).
sources.transcripts.dropped_out_of_windo: {count} transcripts left out because no message falls inside the window.
sources.transcripts.dropped_unreadable: {count} transcripts could not be read (listed above).
sources.transcripts.problem_no_projects: No project is listed in sources.transcripts.include_projects, so no transcript was read. List the project directories to read (their names under the transcripts directory).
sources.transcripts.problem_root_missing: The transcripts directory {root} does not exist, so no transcript was read.
sources.transcripts.problem_project_miss: The project {project} listed in sources.transcripts.include_projects has no directory under {root}.
sources.transcripts.dropped_modified_bef: {count} transcripts not opened because they were last modified before the window opened.
sources.transcripts.problem_root_unreada: The transcripts directory {root} exists but could not be listed, so no transcript was read.
sources.transcripts.problem_project_unre: The project {project} listed in sources.transcripts.include_projects exists under {root} but could not be listed, so none of its transcripts was read.
prompt.curate_parameters_standalone: (brain-kit curate fills in this block at each round: the days to read, the window, the sources with what to read in each, the limits and the kit command.)
prompt.curate_unreadable: The curate prompt could not be loaded ({path}: {detail}). Run brain-kit doctor.
prompt.check_prompts_dir_unreadable: {lang}: the prompts directory could not be read ({dir}).
prompt.check_missing_prompt: prompts/{name}.md ({lang}): missing, and the kit needs it.
prompt.check_prompt_mismatch: prompts/{name}.md: present in {lang} but not in {other}.
prompt.check_prompt_first_line: prompts/{name}.md ({lang}): the first line must be exactly {line}.
prompt.check_prompt_missing_rule: prompts/{name}.md ({lang}): the contract marker for the rule "{rule}" is missing.
prompt.check_prompt_placeholders_differ: prompts/{name}.md: the placeholders differ between {lang} and {other}.
prompt.check_overlay_unreadable: warning: the vault's curate prompt {path} could not be read ({detail}).
prompt.check_overlay_missing_rule: warning: the vault's curate prompt {path} has no contract marker for the rule "{rule}"; a round will run it as written.
prompt.check_overlay_signature_prepended: warning: the vault's curate prompt {path} does not start with {line}; a round will put the signature line in front of it.
prompt.check_overlay_unknown_placeholder: warning: the vault's curate prompt {path} uses the placeholder "{placeholder}", which a round does not fill; it will reach the model as written.
schedule.platform_needs_value: brain-kit schedule: --platform needs a value: systemd, launchd or cron.
schedule.unknown_action: brain-kit schedule: unknown action "{action}"; the actions are install, uninstall and status.
schedule.bad_platform: brain-kit schedule: unknown platform "{platform}"; the platforms are {platforms}.
schedule.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit schedule: "{dir}" is not a directory.
schedule.no_vault: brain-kit schedule: no brain-kit vault found from "{dir}" or any directory above it (looking for {config} and {index}).
schedule.moved: brain-kit schedule: machine.json records the vault at "{recorded}", but this vault is at "{root}". Run brain-kit machine register first, so the entry never runs a round against the wrong place.
schedule.windows_manual: brain-kit schedule: this kit installs no scheduler on Windows yet. Create a Task Scheduler task by hand that runs, every day at {windows}, this command: {command}
schedule.disabled: brain-kit schedule: curate.enabled is false in {file}, so there is nothing to schedule. Set it to true and run install again.
schedule.no_windows: brain-kit schedule: curate.schedule in {file} lists no window, and a timer with no window never runs. List at least one, such as 09:30.
schedule.overnight: brain-kit schedule: curate.schedule in {file} has windows outside the day ({windows}). Windows go from {from} to before {until}: overnight, a sleeping machine fires the round when it wakes, before the network is up. Move them into the day and run install again.
schedule.bad_timezone: brain-kit schedule: vault.timezone in {file} is "{timezone}", which is not a time zone this machine knows (use a name such as Europe/Lisbon). Scheduled with it, the round would run on the wrong clock.
schedule.claude_not_found: brain-kit schedule: claude_bin "{bin}" was not found, in path_extra or on PATH. Point it at the binary with brain-kit machine set claude_bin <path> and run install again.
schedule.unsafe_path: brain-kit schedule: "{path}" has a character this scheduler cannot carry safely (a control character, a colon in a PATH directory, a backslash in a crontab, or a quote or backslash in a program path systemd runs). Nothing was written. Move it to a path without that character, or pick another platform with --platform.
schedule.timezone_differs: brain-kit schedule: this machine's clock ({local}) and the vault's time zone ({vault}) do not keep the same time all year. The scheduler fires on the machine's clock, so the windows are read in the machine's zone, not the vault's.
schedule.dry_crontab_block: --- crontab (this block is added; every other line is kept)
schedule.dry_remove_block: --- crontab (the block {name} is removed; every other line is kept)
schedule.crontab_read_failed: brain-kit schedule: crontab -l failed, so the crontab was not touched: {detail}
schedule.crontab_broken: brain-kit schedule: the crontab has the line that opens the block {name} but not the one that closes it. Fix it with crontab -e; nothing was written.
schedule.nothing_installed: brain-kit schedule: {name} ({platform}) is not installed; nothing to remove.
schedule.status_active: brain-kit schedule: {name} ({platform}) is installed, matches the configuration and is enabled.
schedule.status_not_installed: brain-kit schedule: {name} ({platform}) is not installed. Run brain-kit schedule install.
schedule.status_outdated: brain-kit schedule: {name} ({platform}) is installed but no longer matches the configuration and this machine. Run brain-kit schedule install again.
schedule.status_inactive: brain-kit schedule: {name} ({platform}) is installed but the scheduler does not have it enabled ({detail}). Run brain-kit schedule install again.
schedule.status_no_last_run: Last run: none recorded yet ({file} does not exist).
schedule.status_last_run_unreadable: Last run: {file} could not be read ({detail}).
schedule.cron_line_too_long: brain-kit schedule: a crontab line would be {bytes} bytes, above the {limit} this kit allows (many cron versions refuse the whole crontab near 1000). Shorten path_extra or the vault's path; nothing was written.
schedule.uninstall_unconfirmed: brain-kit schedule: the files of {name} ({platform}) are removed, but the scheduler did not confirm it stopped the timer. Check with systemctl --user list-timers.
schedule.crontab_duplicate: brain-kit schedule: the crontab holds the block {name} more than once. Remove the extra copy with crontab -e; nothing was written.
schedule.crontab_foreign_env: brain-kit schedule: the crontab sets its own environment above the block ({lines}), and those lines apply to the block too: the windows or the shell may not be what this kit wrote.
schedule.found_elsewhere: brain-kit schedule: nothing for {name} under {platform}, but there is an entry under {platforms}. Run the command again with --platform and that name.
schedule.pinned_path: brain-kit schedule: the entry records {path}, a path a version manager or the npx cache can replace or remove; the day it goes, the round stops starting. Prefer a node and a kit at stable paths, or run schedule install again after each upgrade.
curate.usage:
Usage: brain-kit curate [dir] [--dry] [--check] [--keep-stream]

Runs one scheduled curator round, in a fixed order: the machine file, the vault lock, the network, sync, the configuration as synced, the window from the watermark, a clean tree, the round's snapshot, the Claude Code CLI, the sources, then the model, isolated from your own Claude Code settings. Afterwards it checks what the model read, brings the files it proposed back to the default branch, advances the watermark only when every required source was read, writes last-run.json and the log in the state directory, and runs machine.notify_command on any failure.

  --dry          print what the round would do (window, sources, the command line) and stop: no lock, no sync, nothing written; the configuration is read from the working tree as it is now
  --check        run every step up to the model and stop: print the plan and the prompt's size, never call the model
  --keep-stream  also keep the model's raw output in the state directory

Exit codes: 0 done or nothing to do, 1 failed, 2 not a vault or bad setting, 3 proposed but the pull request is not open, 4 a required source was not read, 69 no network or model unavailable, 75 postponed (lock held, dirty tree, diverged branch).
curate.path_not_a_directory: brain-kit curate: {dir} is not a directory
curate.no_vault: brain-kit curate: no vault at or above {dir} (looked for {config} or a root {index})
curate.machine_invalid: brain-kit curate: this machine's settings cannot be used, so no round runs: {detail}
curate.internal_error: brain-kit curate: the round stopped on an unexpected error: {detail}
curate.network_failed: brain-kit curate: no network after waiting {waited} s ({attempts} attempts); the round did not start.
curate.network_did_not_wait: brain-kit curate: the network check answered in {ms} ms on its first try; it may be checking something other than the connection (see brain-kit doctor).
curate.interrupted: brain-kit curate: the round was stopped by {signal}; the model and everything it started were killed.
curate.sync_postponed: brain-kit curate: postponed, sync could not bring the default branch level with its remote (see the message above); nothing was curated.
curate.sync_failed: brain-kit curate: sync failed (see the message above); nothing was curated.
curate.config_invalid: brain-kit curate: the vault's configuration, as synced, cannot be used: {detail}
curate.prompt_outside: brain-kit curate: {setting} points at {path}, outside the vault; the round only runs a prompt that is part of the reviewed vault.
curate.watermark_unreadable: brain-kit curate: cannot read the watermark {file}: {detail}. Fix or remove the file; nothing was curated.
curate.bad_timezone: brain-kit curate: vault.timezone in {file} is {timezone}, not a time zone this machine knows; the round has no days to read.
curate.watermark_future: brain-kit curate: the watermark of {source} says {day}, later than yesterday ({yesterday}); a clock ran ahead and real days would be skipped. Run {command} and the next round reads them.
curate.up_to_date: brain-kit curate: already up to date, every source was swept through yesterday.
curate.dirty: brain-kit curate: postponed, the working tree has changes the round did not make: {files}. Commit, propose or discard them, and the next round runs.
curate.cli_unusable: brain-kit curate: the Claude Code CLI cannot run a round: {problem}
curate.source_unknown: brain-kit curate: {setting} names {sources}, which this version cannot read; no watermark moved.
curate.source_skipped: brain-kit curate: the best-effort source {source} has no reader in this version and was skipped.
curate.source_misconfigured: brain-kit curate: the required source {source} is not set up ({problems}); fix {setting}. No watermark moved.
curate.nothing_to_curate: brain-kit curate: nothing to curate for {days}; the model was not started.
curate.check_done: brain-kit curate: check done, the model was not called.
curate.dry_header: Dry run: no lock taken, nothing synced, nothing written. The configuration is read from the working tree as it is now, which a real round would sync first.
curate.cleanup_restored: brain-kit curate: brought back to the default branch, as pushed: {paths}
curate.cleanup_changed: brain-kit curate: changed after the push, left as they are: {paths}
curate.isolation_failed: brain-kit curate: the model was not isolated from your own Claude Code settings and was stopped: {problems}
curate.model_timed_out: brain-kit curate: the model ran longer than {minutes} minutes and was killed.
curate.model_unavailable: brain-kit curate: the model is unavailable (an API or login error, result {subtype}): {detail}
curate.model_failed: brain-kit curate: the model run failed (result {subtype}, exit {code}): {detail}
curate.source_unread: brain-kit curate: a required source was not read in full (read/listed): {sources}. The day stays open.
curate.record_invalid: brain-kit curate: the round's record {file} in {dir} cannot be read; it and the files are left as they are for you to look at.
curate.leftovers: brain-kit curate: the round left changes it did not propose: {paths}. They stay for you to look at, and the day stays open.
curate.not_opened: brain-kit curate: pushed but the pull request is not open for {branches}; finish it with the command propose printed.
curate.done_proposed: brain-kit curate: done, {count} file(s) proposed on {branch}.
curate.done_nothing: brain-kit curate: done, nothing was proposed.
curate.not_advanced: brain-kit curate: the watermark of {source} did not move ({reason}).
prompt.check_prompt_outside: the vault's curate.prompt in {file} points at {path}, outside the vault; a round refuses to run it.
curate.days_remaining: brain-kit curate: this round reads through {last}; {count} more day(s) remain, and the next round continues from there.
curate.params.remaining: {count} newer open day(s) are left for the next round; this round curates only the days above.
curate.sync_diverged: brain-kit curate: the default branch has diverged from its remote (see the message above); a person must reconcile them, and nothing was curated.
